deep.reconstruction:
Context: on fol. 6r Riemann adopts Newton's view that at every point of space there is a definite cause (the resultant gravitational force). He locates this cause in the motion of a substance (Stoff) that fills all space continuously, with the velocity equal in size and direction to the force. Light and heat crossing empty space must also be motions of this substance.

This page contains no derivation. It sets up the program and the notation.

(1) Hypothesis of superposition. The actual velocity field of the substance in empty space is the sum of two parts: the motion that explains gravitation and the motion that explains light.

(2) Division of the work into two parts.
- (i) A mathematical part: find the laws of these substance motions that the phenomena require.
- (ii) A metaphysical part: find the causes from which those motions can be explained.

(3) Methodological remark on part (ii). The goal is not to explain things by causes that tend to change the distance between two substance points, i.e. central attractive or repulsive forces between point pairs. Riemann argues why that method became general in physics:
- not because it is immediately evident or especially rational;
- not because it is especially easy (setting aside electricity and gravity);
- but because Newton's law of attraction was long treated as needing no further explanation, against Newton's own opinion.

The note (+) points to a Newton quotation; compare Hypotheses non fingo on the previous page.

(4) Section I, notation.
- Cartesian coordinates x1, x2, x3 and time t.
- Gravitational part of the velocity: u = (u1, u2, u3).
- Light part: w = (w1, w2, w3).
- Actual velocity: v = (v1, v2, v3).
- Hence v = u + w, componentwise v_i = u_i + w_i.

(5) Density. Riemann states, as a result still to come from the laws of motion, that a substance uniformly dense at one instant stays uniformly dense everywhere. He therefore normalizes the density to 1.

Implicit (my addition): by the continuity equation d(rho)/dt + div(rho v) = 0, constant rho = 1 requires div v = 0.
- On the next page, div u = 0 outside ponderable matter, since u = grad V with V harmonic there.
- Light waves in vacuum are transverse, so div w = 0.
- At ponderable elements, div u * dx1 dx2 dx3 = -4 pi dm. Ponderable matter therefore acts as a sink of the substance. This matches the idea in Riemann's published Naturphilosophie fragments that ponderable bodies absorb the ether.
errors: No computational errors; the page has no computations.

The claim that uniform density is preserved is stated in advance ('wie sich ... ergeben wird'). It holds only where div v = 0. With div u = -4 pi rho_mass (next page), density constancy needs a sink interpretation at ponderable matter. Otherwise the continuity equation would give d(rho)/dt = 4 pi rho_mass there. This is a physical assumption Riemann leaves implicit on this page.

results.what: Hypothesis that gravity and light are both motions of one space-filling incompressible medium, with velocity = superposition of a gravitational (potential) part u and a light (wave) part w; normalization of density to 1
results.modern_name: Unified ether/continuum-mechanical model of gravitation and light (sink/flow model of gravity; Helmholtz-type split of a velocity field into irrotational plus solenoidal parts)
results.usually_credited_to: Ether-flow gravity: Fatio/Le Sage-type and sink models (Riemann, later Bjerknes, Challis). This text itself is Riemann's posthumously published 'Gravitation und Licht' / Naturphilosophie fragment (Werke 1876).

results.what: Methodological rejection of action-at-a-distance central forces as ultimate explanations; Newton's law was taken as unexplainable against Newton's own opinion
results.modern_name: Critique of action at a distance in favour of field/contact action
results.usually_credited_to: Faraday, Maxwell, and Riemann (published in his Werke, Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the programmatic opening of Riemann's known Naturphilosophie fragment on gravitation and light, published by Dedekind and Weber in the Werke (1876). It contains only notation and methodology, no new mathematics.

checkable.sympy: x1,x2,x3=symbols('x1 x2 x3'); r=sqrt(x1**2+x2**2+x3**2); V=1/r; u=[diff(V,x) for x in (x1,x2,x3)]; simplify(sum(diff(u[i],[x1,x2,x3][i]) for i in range(3)))
checkable.asserts: Outside the attracting mass, the gravitational part u = grad V with V = 1/r has zero divergence. This is consistent with constant density away from matter.

checkable.sympy: x1,x2,x3,t,k,c=symbols('x1 x2 x3 t k c'); w=[sin(k*(x3-c*t)),0,0]; simplify(diff(w[0],x1)+diff(w[1],x2)+diff(w[2],x3))
checkable.asserts: A transverse plane wave (displacement along x1, propagation along x3) is divergence-free. So the light part w does not change the density.
With rho = 1 constant, the continuity equation d(rho)/dt + div(rho v) = 0 reduces to div v = 0. This is the condition behind Riemann's claim that uniform density is preserved.
